description: Unknown kinds, unknown JSON members, unknown blyg:* XML elements and reserved constructs are ignored without rejecting the containing document.
given: A feed or item document carrying constructs the reader does not implement (an unknown kind, an extra JSON member, an unknown blyg:* element).

expect.outcome: The reader ignores each unknown construct and continues; the containing document is never rejected.
asserts: Any 0.x value of the blyg key is accepted and the ignore-unknown rules apply.
An unknown kind is an unknown construct, not a parse failure.
Only the individual unknown construct is dropped, never the container.

description: Readers MUST NOT gate any behaviour on level, generator, generator_url, or the self-asserted changelog generated flag.
given: Two blygs with different informative level/generator values and a changelog entry carrying generated:true.

expect.outcome: Both are processed identically; no parsing, feature selection or trust decision reads those fields.
asserts: level, generator and generator_url are informative only.
The changelog generated flag is self-asserted and never gated on.
Behaviour is identical across levels.

description: Everything is scoped to the origin: ids, authors, transclusion ids and trust do not transfer across origins.
given: The same item id (or an equal author object) observed at two different origins.

expect.outcome: The two are held apart as distinct origin-scoped entities; a publisher finding one id at two imported origins treats it as ambiguous.
asserts: Ids are scoped to the origin they were learned from.
Equal author values at different origins are not the same entity.
A transclusion id is scoped to its origin when present, else to the document's own origin.

description: Publishers SHOULD cap fragment content at 2000 chars, but a reader MUST NOT reject a long fragment.
given: A fragment whose content_md exceeds 2000 characters.

expect.outcome: The reader accepts and reconciles the long fragment; the cap is a publisher-side recommendation only.
asserts: The 2000-char cap is a SHOULD on publishers.
Readers MUST NOT reject long fragments.
No truncation of stored content occurs.

description: Clients that store or re-emit item JSON carry author verbatim, never synthesized or rewritten, and never reject an item over it.
given: An imported item whose author object contains nonstandard members.

expect.outcome: The author object is stored and re-emitted byte-for-byte; the item is accepted regardless of its contents.
asserts: author is carried verbatim through store and re-emit (where re-emit is permitted at all).
An item is never rejected over its author contents.
Equal author values across origins are not merged.

description: Item documents are ground truth; the feed is a lossy notification signal that never mutates state directly.
given: A feed whose entry disagrees with the authoritative items/{id}.json document.

expect.outcome: The feed triggers a fetch; only the fetched document advances state, and the feed's claims are discarded.
asserts: The feed is a cheap trigger, never ground truth.
Only a fetched document advances stored state.
A poll failure leaves stored state unaltered.

description: Roll-up is by blyg:id: the highest version wins, ties broken by updated.
given: Multiple observations of one id at the same origin with differing versions (and a same-version tie).

expect.outcome: The row with the highest version is presented; equal versions are ordered by updated.
asserts: Highest version wins.
Same-version ties break by updated.
Roll-up is per origin.

description: When the feed window has been missed, the reader backfills from items/index.json (feed-window gaps fall back to an index diff).
given: A reader that was offline across more publish events than the feed window holds.

expect.outcome: The reader diffs items/index.json against local watermarks and fetches only the missing documents.
asserts: The archive index is the reconciliation surface.
The feed is only a cheap trigger.
Backfill fetches only documents missing locally.

description: An unparseable feed goes straight to an index diff; an unparseable entry is skipped individually and never rejects the containing feed.
given: A feed containing one malformed <item> among otherwise valid entries.

expect.outcome: The malformed entry is skipped; the rest of the feed is processed, and a wholly unparseable feed falls back to the index diff.
asserts: Entry-level parse failures are isolated.
The containing feed is never rejected outright.
A wholly unparseable feed triggers an index diff.

description: A 404 on items/index.json from an otherwise-live blyg is nonconforming; the reader falls back to feed-window-only operation and marks the subscription lossy.
given: A blyg whose manifest and feed resolve but whose items/index.json returns 404.

expect.outcome: The subscription operates from the feed window alone and is surfaced as lossy.
asserts: The missing index is recorded as nonconforming/lossy.
Feed-window-only operation continues.
The condition is surfaced to the user.

description: A poll failure never alters stored item state.
given: A transient network or 5xx failure during a poll.

expect.outcome: Stored items and watermarks are untouched; only the polling schedule (backoff) is affected.
asserts: Failures do not mutate item state or watermarks.
Failures do not delete stored content.
Retry is scheduled with backoff.

description: A fetched document whose version is below the watermark MUST NOT be silently adopted; the reader surfaces it and MAY offer a user-confirmed reset.
given: A fetched item document whose version is lower than the locally stored watermark.

expect.outcome: The regression is surfaced as a discrepancy; the older version is not silently adopted; a user-confirmed reset may be offered.
asserts: Version regression is loud, not silent.
The stale document is not adopted without confirmation.
The watermark is not lowered automatically.

description: Same version but a different content_hash is a stealth edit: adopt the fetched content, record/surface the discrepancy, and leave the watermark unchanged.
given: A fetched document at the same version as stored but with a different content_hash.

expect.outcome: The fetched content is adopted, a stealth-edit discrepancy is recorded and surfaced, and the watermark stays the same.
asserts: Content is adopted despite the hash change.
The discrepancy is recorded and surfaced.
The watermark is unchanged.

description: Readers verify content_hash against content_md on import; a mismatch is a discrepancy signal and the content is adopted anyway.
given: A fetched document whose content_hash does not match sha256(content_md).

expect.outcome: The mismatch is recorded and surfaced; the document content is adopted regardless.
asserts: content_hash is recomputed over content_md on import.
A mismatch is a discrepancy, not a rejection.
The content is still adopted.

description: A withdrawal endcap rolls the item up to null: withdrawn content stops being presented and is deleted unless a pin authorizes retention.
given: A reader holding an unpinned withdrawn item, then fetching its kind=withdrawn endcap.

expect.outcome: The item rolls up to null, drops from the local archive, and the stored copy is deleted; the endcap document stays 200 at the origin.
asserts: A withdrawal endcap is roll-up-to-null.
Unpinned withdrawn content is dropped from the local archive.
The id is remembered so a later version is the item returning.

description: A pin is the only thing that may be retained past withdrawal; a pin-retained snapshot stays a valid transclusion source.
given: An item withdrawn after one of its versions was pinned and locally retained.

expect.outcome: The pinned snapshot is retained with attribution and remains usable as a transclusion source; local hoarding beyond pins is nonconforming.
asserts: Retention follows a pin only.
A pin-retained snapshot remains a valid transclusion source.
An unretained withdrawn item is not a transclusion source.

description: Withdrawal is reversible: a later publish event under the same id is the item returning.
given: An item that was withdrawn and later republished under the same id at a higher version.

expect.outcome: The reader rolls up to the new version and presents the item again under the same identity.
asserts: The id is permanent across withdrawal and return.
A higher-version document is reconciled as the return.
Identity and origin are unchanged.

description: Legacy L0 wrapping: synthetic ids are never valid blyg ids, L0 rows are never transclusion sources, and a changed GUID is a local version bump.
given: A plain RSS feed (no blyg namespace) subscribed in legacy mode.

expect.outcome: Entries are wrapped as L0 rows with synthetic non-blyg ids; the same GUID with changed content bumps a local version; there is no withdrawal and no archive index.
asserts: Synthetic L0 ids are never valid blyg ids and are never exported or re-emitted.
An L0 row is never a transclusion source; a reply to it is a {url} stub.
RSS has no versions; changed content under one GUID is a local version bump.

description: Ordering the merged reading surface is the reader's own policy; a skewed or future-dated origin cannot permanently dominate the display order.
given: A merged timeline across origins, one of which publishes future-dated or clock-skewed items.

expect.outcome: The reader's policy keeps one origin from permanently dominating the order.
asserts: Display ordering is a reader policy, not a protocol rule.
Future-dated items cannot permanently pin the top of the surface.
Ranking/profile inputs remain private (spec-external, SUK-145).
